title: Power Automate: share Process license capacity across cloud flows with flow groups
summary: The briefing's capacity limits, licensing, rollout description and creation controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The governance checklist still names monitoring checks that have no corresponding controls-table row; this is a minor completeness finding.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Flow groups share Power Automate Process license capacity across cloud flows.
claims.quote: A flow group lets you share the capacity of a Power Automate Process license across multiple cloud flows, instead of dedicating a license to each flow separately.

claims.claim: A flow group can contain up to 25 flows.
claims.quote: Flows per group | 25 total flow members. Each parent or child flow you add to the group counts separately.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Eligible cloud flows must be solution-aware.
claims.quote: Cloud flows stored in a solution (solution-aware).

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A flow group takes one Process license.
claims.quote: Process licenses per group | 1 (250,000 actions per day). Stacking isn't available for flow groups.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each Process license provides up to 250,000 actions per day.
claims.quote: Each Process license includes up to 250,000 actions per day (shown as Power Platform Requests in admin center reports). You can stack licenses on one flow, or share one license across a flow group.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Member flows consume a shared 250,000-action daily pool measured at group level rather than per flow.
claims.quote: When you assign it to a flow group, all flows in the group share that 250,000-action daily pool. Consumption is measured against the group total, not per individual flow.

claims.claim: A flow group is scoped to a single environment.
claims.quote: Scope | Single environment

claims.claim: Process license stacking is not available for flow groups.
claims.quote: License stacking (assigning multiple Process licenses for higher capacity) isn't available for flow groups.

claims.claim: A flow can belong to only one group at a time.
claims.quote: Group membership | A flow can belong to only one group at a time

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Adding a parent flow does not automatically add its child flows.
claims.quote: Parent and child flows are separate group members; adding a parent flow to a group doesn't add its child flows automatically.

claims.quote: 25 total flow members. Each parent or child flow you add to the group counts separately.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A child flow left outside the group does not inherit the group's shared capacity.
claims.quote: Only flows that you explicitly add to the group use its shared Process capacity.

claims.claim: Cloud flows outside a solution are not eligible.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The flow group pages publish no separate flow group licence, price or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups pricing meter. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/flow-groups and /power-automate/create-flow-group in full; both require Process capacity but name no separate group licence, price or meter.

claims.claim: The flow group pages do not publish a price for the Process license itself.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups pricing meter. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/flow-groups and /power-automate/create-flow-group in full; neither gives a Process license price.

claims.claim: For a flow needing more than 250,000 daily actions, Learn directs assigning Process licenses directly to that flow.
claims.quote: If a flow needs more than 250,000 actions per day, assign Process licenses directly to that individual flow instead.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes savings through sharing Process capacity rather than dedicating capacity to every workflow.
claims.quote: share Process license capacity across up to 25 cloud flows, optimizing license allocation and reducing costs for organizations operating higher-volume workflows that don't need their own dedicated capacity.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that arrival changes existing flows automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups existing flows rollout. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/flow-groups and /power-automate/create-flow-group; they describe explicit creation and membership, not automatic changes to existing flows.

claims.claim: Learn describes no new data access introduced by flow groups.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups data access. Read learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/flow-groups and /power-automate/create-flow-group in full; both describe licensing and group management, without a new data-access mechanism.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature documentation does not specify a separate creation role or approval step beyond maker permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups flowgroup creation permissions security roles approval restrict. Opened /power-automate/flow-groups and /power-automate/create-flow-group; no additional group-specific role or approval is stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn recommends moving a consistently dominant member out and assigning it a dedicated Process license.
claims.quote: Review consumption regularly. If one flow consistently dominates the group's capacity, move it out and assign a dedicated Process license to that flow.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The flow group pages do not specify what happens to other members when the shared pool is exhausted.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups capacity exceeded suspended; Power Automate flow groups shared pool exhausted what happens member flows daily limit. Read both flow group pages and licensing FAQ excerpts; no group-exhaustion response for other members is specified.

claims.claim: Learn mentions flows regularly exceeding 100,000 actions per day as candidates for dedicated Process licensing.

claims.where: controls[1]; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: No tenant or environment switch to disable flow groups is documented on the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups disable admin setting Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell; Power Automate flow groups disable tenant environment settings. Read both feature pages and tenant-settings/PowerShell/CLI search excerpts; no group-disable switch found.

claims.claim: No group-specific admin creation restriction beyond maker permissions is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate flow groups flowgroup creation permissions security roles approval restrict. Read both feature pages and role-guidance search excerpts; general maker controls exist, but no additional flow-group-specific creation setting was found.

claims.claim: The documented table-create call does not describe assigning Process capacity.
claims.quote: Searched: capacity and licens in the fetched flowgroup reference. Its Create message creates a row; the reference lists a flowcapacityassignment relationship but gives no Process-capacity assignment procedure for this POST.

claims.claim: The documented table-create call does not describe adding member flows.
claims.quote: Searched: flowgroup table messages and writable columns in its reference. Create is POST /flowgroups; no member-add procedure is specified for that call. The maker instructions explicitly document Add flow.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center has a Power Automate Usage report.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Usage page in the Power Platform admin center shows which users and flows in your tenant are exceeding their daily Power Automate action or request limits.

claims.claim: Learn recommends the usage report for deciding which flows need dedicated capacity.
claims.quote: The report helps you decide which flows need dedicated capacity and which can share a group.

claims.claim: The Usage report is a consumption-reporting surface rather than a capacity-limit setting.
claims.quote: Users over their daily limit: a list of users whose Power Automate action or request consumption exceeds their daily entitlement, with a usage trend over time and the top consumers called out.

claims.claim: The flow group rollout note gives no regional completion dates.
claims.quote: Searched: flow groups rollout completion. Read learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/create-flow-group; it says rollout starts in July 2026 and continues across regions, without regional completion dates.

claims.where: Governance guidance; Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: The governance checklist's Analytics and group-consumption monitoring checks have no controls-table row.
claims.quote: Guidance: "Identify candidate flows by their daily action count" and "Review group consumption regularly". Controls: "The Analytics usage check and the regular group-consumption review ... have no monitoring row in the table above."
claims.fix: The Before rollout step 'Identify candidate flows by their daily action count' and After rollout step 'Review group consumption regularly' have no corresponding monitoring row in the controls table. This is a checklist/table completeness gap, not an instruction to add rows during correction.
